correctness.rationale: The family of all feasible named bipartitions is exhausted by testing each of 4096 vertex subsets, with 60 valid six-subsets. A seven-subset has at least 8 induced edges and cannot be a forest; a six-forest has 5 edges and maximum degree 2 since each vertex neighborhood is a pentagon, hence induces P6. The two standalone verification programs use separate graph representations and separate forest predicates; both reproduce 120 legal exchanges, degree 4 at every state, all 60 BFS shells (1,4,12,17,16,9,1), complement as the unique distance-6 state, and the complete 1770-pair Johnson-distance table with 420 one-detour pairs. Python separately verifies girth six and original-edge locality. The explicit graph relabeling between encodings has been checked.

Complete relevant published RESULT texts and the original historical literature were compared against the new facet-exchange graph, Johnson distance law and complementary antipode statement. value.rationale: This is a canonical, non-arbitrary minimal two-class vertex-arboricity/path-factor problem on the regular icosahedron. Its natural move operation requires preserving both induced forests. The sharp one-detour law, 420-pair exception census, unique complementary antipodes and automatic locality of legal swaps give a full new geometric account of how optimal partitions move; these are not merely recomputations of the published 60-object count or homotopy. No general theorem beyond this motivated finite object is asserted.
